newsitem.title: UK: UK clears way for Lloyds Chemist bidding war.
newsitem.headline: UK clears way for Lloyds Chemist bidding war.

text.p: Britain's Department of Trade and Industry announced it accepted undertakings from Germany's Gehe and Britain's Unichem to sell parts of Lloyds Chemists should either acquire the pharmacy group eyed by both.
The Department of Trade and Industry had said in July that bids by either UniChem or Gehe could only go ahead if some of Lloyds Chemists' wholesaling businesses were sold off.
The condition was imposed after rival bids from the two firms had been referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
The offers automatically lapsed due to the referral but fresh bids are widely expected to be launched now the government approved the undertakings from UniChem and Gehe.

"I am satisfied that UniChem and Gehe have given undertakings as required...to remedy the competition concerns identified by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission," said John Taylor, minister for corporate and consumer affairs.
